result.rationale: The diff changes updateEvent/deleteEvent fallbacks to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches, so the expression evaluates to `undefined` — exactly what the finding states. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Behavior change is verifiable directly from the diff lines.

record.issue_text: [P1] Google updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: find compares against undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy, losing previous destinationCalendar?.externalId fallback and sending calendarId: undefined

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new fallback logic for `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` is incorrect: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares `cal.externalId` to `undefined` and therefore will typically return `undefined` even if `destinationCalendar` contains entries. This removes the previous fallback behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it was a single object) and can result in failing to pick a destination calendar ID when `externalCalendarId` is not provided.
